newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says will not use forex to boost export.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says will not use forex to boost export.

text.p: Indonesia's central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said on Friday he would not use foreign exchange rates to boost the country's exports.
"I am not a true believer of using foreign exchange rates to boost exports," he told a Southeast Asian economic meeting.
He said exchange rates were only supporting elements in boosting trade along with factors such as productivity.

Indonesia is seeking to increase exports while cutting back on imports in a bid to reduce its current account deficit, which is forecast to widen to $8.7 billion in fiscal 1996/97 (April/March) from $7 billion in 1995/96.
International Monetary Fund managing director Michel Camdessus said on Thursday he expected Indonesia's economic growth this year to be lower than the 8.07 percent posted in 1995.
